promises: Plain files you can edit by hand
tagline: A signed-in What's New page that gets a new entry every session
use_when: You want signed-in users to see what changed in your app, written from plain files, and want Claude to add an entry whenever it ships something they would notice.
try_it: Use the changelog skill to add a signed-in /changelog page to this app and log what we shipped today.

features.label: A What's New Page
features.sub: A changelog page inside your app
features.title: A changelog page inside your app
features.what: Signed-in users get a /changelog page listing what changed and when. The skill is a spec, not a package: Claude builds the page in your own language and framework from its file format, parsing rules and behavior. People learn about new features from the app itself instead of an email they skipped.

features.title: One plain text file per app, newest first

features.label: An Entry Each Session
features.sub: Claude adds a dated entry when it ships something
features.title: Claude adds a dated entry when it ships something
features.what: At the end of any session that shipped something users would notice, Claude adds an entry under today's date without being asked. The changelog stays current because nobody has to remember it.

features.title: Features and real fixes, not tidy-up work

features.label: Tests for the Quiet Bugs
features.sub: Tests catch the bugs that fail without errors
features.title: Tests catch the bugs that fail without errors
features.what: Setup includes tests for the page, the sign-in gate, the month archive and the file parser, including a bad heading and text rendering outside its bullet. Those bugs would otherwise fail silently.

features.label: Colors That Survive the Build
features.sub: Theme colors are spelled out so a CSS build keeps them
features.title: Theme colors are spelled out so CSS keeps them
features.what: If your CSS tooling scans source files for complete class names, each color theme is written out as full class names rather than pieced together. A build that strips unused styles can then see them, so the timeline doesn't lose its colors in production.
